overview: The MPS Budget process involves the annual formulation and approval of operating funds for Medford Public Schools, covering everything from staffing levels to capital maintenance. Between May 2024 and May 2026, the body has navigated significant fiscal challenges, including multi-million dollar deficits and rising contractual costs. The process includes statutory public hearings and joint coordination sessions with the Medford City Council to align revenue projections. At the most recent meeting in May 2026, the body approved a preliminary budget proposal for the 2027 fiscal year that balances base budget increases with targeted net reductions.

threads.name: FY25 Budget Process
threads.summary: In early 2024, the budget faced a $2.7 million deficit despite $2.3 million in proposed cuts to staff and programs. Finance Director Gerry McCue detailed rising operational costs and the potential loss of 17.4 full-time positions. Following significant public pressure, the committee approved a level-service request of $79,399,774 to be submitted to city officials.

threads.name: FY26 Budget Process
threads.summary: Planning for the 2026 fiscal year began with joint revenue projections showing a certified free cash balance of $28.3 million. Administrators presented an $87,583,000 preliminary budget that accounted for enrollment increases and salary adjustments. Unlike previous years, the public hearing for this budget saw no public testimony for or against the proposal before it was approved as the formal municipal request.

threads.name: FY27 Budget Process
threads.summary: The fiscal year 2027 budget proposal included a $4.1 million base budget increase. However, the finance team also presented $3.3 million in net reductions. The committee approved the preliminary recommendations while making it a priority to restore a vacant inclusion specialist position if funds are available.

threads.name: Staffing and Personnel Levels
threads.summary: Budgetary constraints have frequently centered on the preservation of student-facing roles. In 2024, dozens of community members protested cuts to nurses, drama coordinators, and administrative assistants. By 2026, the focus shifted to maintaining specialized positions, such as inclusion specialists, amidst ongoing net reductions.

threads.name: Inter-governmental Coordination
threads.summary: The School Committee and City Council established joint rules to govern shared sessions regarding fiscal planning. These meetings involve reviews of the budget calendar and requests for formal documentation of revenue estimates from the city's Chief Financial Officer. These sessions aim to reconcile city-wide revenue forecasts with school-specific cost drivers like health insurance premiums.

threads.name: Facilities and Programmatic Expansion
threads.summary: While managing operating deficits, the committee also makes budgetary decisions regarding long-term facility usage and program pilots. This included approving the co-location of the Curtis-Tufts School with the high school and directing funds for a new alternative education pilot for at-risk students. Additionally, the committee has sought to expand Career Technical Education (CTE) offerings through coordination with the MSBA feasibility study.
